title: Finite Q3 commutator-sum Lie-Trotter defect and two-orientation history bound
question: For the declared finite Q3 split Hamiltonians, does an explicit commutator-sum Lie-Trotter defect bound control both product orders and both time signs, and does the induced two-orientation history admit the corresponding finite operator-norm bound?
method: Reuse the hash-pinned finite Q3 oscillator fixture from EXP-001161 and reconstruct every onsite and bond term as a self-adjoint finite matrix on volumes 2, 4 and 6.
Use tensor support locality to set disjoint commutators to zero and evaluate each overlapping commutator on its union support; compare one full-matrix embedding per volume.
Apply the bounded unitary Duhamel interpolation bound ||S_delta-exp(delta sum H_j)|| <= delta^2 sum_{j<k}||[H_j,H_k]||/2 and unitary telescoping over N steps.
Propagate the right, left and difference cubic-multiplier histories and check ||V_split(M)-V_exact(M)|| <= delta^3 C_V N(N-1)||M||/2 for both split orders and time signs.
Independently rebuild all matrices and compare commutator sums, volume summaries, bound slacks and scope flags; compile Lean R332 for the exact rational coefficients and finite k-sum factor.
finding: Primary 225/225 and independent 108/108 assertions pass over 108 finite history rows; the integrated verifier passes 20/20 and Lean R332 compiles. The commutator sums are C_2=1.6175067619642274, C_4=6.4700270478569095 and C_6=11.322547333749593, with per-site values 0.8087533809821137, 1.6175067619642274 and 1.887091222291599. The fixed-cutoff envelope C_V<=2*(overlapping term pairs)*K_n^2 passes with overlap counts 2, 12 and 24 and K_n approximately 2.25. The minimum unitary and history bound slacks are 0.0005037788211846098 and 0.0005338593106679935; primary and independent aggregate values agree within 4e-16.
decision_reason: The finite Q3 split-to-exact bridge now has an explicit bounded-matrix commutator-sum rate, and the same rate yields a separate two-sided history estimate retaining both noncommuting multiplier orientations. The fixed oscillator-cutoff locality argument gives only a finite-cutoff volume-linear envelope; the observed C_V/V values are diagnostics and do not establish cutoff-uniformity, a common unbounded domain, or a thermodynamic QFT dynamics.
boundary: Finite oscillator dimension three, volumes 2, 4 and 6, source pair [0,1], one probe site per volume, horizon 1/3, step counts 3, 6 and 12, two term orders and time signs -1,+1 only. No infinite-dimensional operator-domain theorem, cutoff-uniform bound, direct D/delta-D Cauchy estimate, exhaustion independence, common alpha, OS/KMS/GNS reconstruction, gap, continuum, C6, Sector A or Pre-A conclusion.
next_action: Derive a cutoff-aware analytic finite-volume rate on a specified common core and test whether the local commutator coefficient can be replaced by a source- and volume-uniform energy/state-weighted bound. If K_n or the domain grows uncontrollably with cutoff, record that exact route-local obstruction and keep common-alpha and QFT reconstruction open.
open: common unbounded operator domain and core density
source/beta/volume-uniform direct D and delta-D Cauchy
gap, continuum, C6, Sector A and Pre-A

adversarial_review.check: The unitary Duhamel interpolation and pairwise commutator sum are used as an inequality; no empirical convergence slope is substituted.
Onsite and bond terms are explicitly hermitianized before exponentiation, and their sum is checked against the pinned full Hamiltonian.
Disjoint tensor supports are zero by construction; overlapping local norms are compared with a full-matrix commutator residual on every declared volume.
The history bound retains the factor two from the two-sided adjoint difference and the exact sum of k=0,...,N-1; it is checked separately for right, left and commutator multipliers.
The 2*overlap_pairs*K_n^2 envelope is explicitly labelled fixed-cutoff; C_V/V is reported but no cutoff- or volume-uniform theorem is inferred.
Finite bounded matrices do not supply a common unbounded core, direct D/delta-D Cauchy, exhaustion, common alpha, OS/KMS/GNS dynamics, a gap, continuum, C6, Sector A or Pre-A closure.

qft_interface.closed: A finite commutator-sum Lie-Trotter rate and its two-orientation history consequence are verified for the declared bounded Q3 matrices, with a fixed-cutoff volume-linear envelope.
qft_interface.open: Cutoff-uniform analytic rate, common domain, thermodynamic history, direct D/delta-D Cauchy, exhaustion, common alpha, OS/KMS/GNS, gap, continuum and Pre-A remain open.
qft_interface.tect_boundary: Auxiliary C6/Q3 evidence only; no TECT production owner, physical-empty reference or Sector-A closure is supplied.

no_overclaim: This finite audit proves only bounded-matrix inequalities and a fixed-cutoff locality envelope. It does not prove a thermodynamic QFT dynamics or close any C6, Sector A or Pre-A gate.
